svg.aria-label: What openDMT3's card reader library does inside the game's process. The game loads CRT_R1.dll by name before its own code runs: its own calls are openDMT3's, and the game's other calls here are turned to openDMT3's in its import table, which call the real ones. At Direct3D 9's Present: frames held to 60.0 a second, locked to the song's music (hooks.c, logic.c); the picture's passes, anti-aliasing then the upscale filter, with the safety net (post.c, shaders/); and the in-game layer drawn over the picture (layer.c, look.c, text.c), to the graphics card and the screen. DirectSound: the chosen output, and the music held and faded while a panel is open (sound.c). GetKeyboardState and GetCursorPos: the in-game layer's keys and clicks never reach the game, and the pointer meets the game pixel under it (hooks.c, layer.c, logic.c). The game's file calls: openDMT3's files in place of the few it changes, the game folder only read (files.c, redirect.c). The card reader's own calls: the card number the launcher wrote, so the game logs that player in (crt_r1.c).

The game loads its card reader library, CRT_R1.dll, by name before its own code runs: openDMT3's, in native/cardreader.
Its own calls are openDMT3's; the others at the left are turned to it in the game's import table, and call the real ones.
